correctness.rationale: The 16 exceptional curves and 10 conic classes of the blow-up of five general points are the stated classical lists. Pairing with F_i=L−E_i gives a vertical index set of size zero on Q (the empty set), size two on L_ab (indices a,b), and size four on E_a (all indices except a). Pairing with G_i=−K−F_i gives the complementary indicator since (−K)·C=1. These are exactly the even-weight five-bit strings. Vertical exceptional curves belong to reducible fibers; a fiber cannot consist solely of a multiple of an exceptional curve, since its square would be negative. The independent parity reconstruction and exact integer Smith and determinant calculations give 1^15,5,20^4,80,320^4 at both a curve sink and a pencil sink. The determinant is 2^36 * 5^10 = 671088640000000000, nonzero, and the degrees 5 and 8 give 80 edges. The exponent is 320. The submitted Euclidean code uses integral unimodular operations, with tracked transformations and exact determinant checks; the independent computation did not use it.
residual_risks: Uses the classical complex quartic del Pezzo blow-up and conic-class classification; no arithmetic descent is claimed.

evidence: At 5, eliminate 8I instead, obtaining 40I−BB^T up to a unit. Since 16 is a 5-unit, split off the constant direction and work on sum-zero vectors. The matrix there is annihilated by (t−32)(t−40), with eigenvalue multiplicities 5 and 10. Since 32−40 is a unit, integral polynomial projectors split these summands over Z_(5). Thus its 5-primary group is (Z/5)^10.
There are no other primes by the immediate tree product. Combining this with the multipartite 2-primary result gives exactly 5,20^4,80,320^4.
